standard_prerequisites: the dilatations theorem (theorem-dilatations-general of the same chapter) and the correspondence between f : X' -> X and g : W -> X_{/T}
etale f gives etale formal completion (lemma-map-completions-etale of the same chapter)
the reduced induced closed subspace Z on T, its infinitesimal neighbourhoods Z_n, and X_{/T} = colim Z_n
the identification of f^{-1}(Z_n) with X' x_X Z_n and etaleness of its map to Z_n from the assumed etaleness of g
etaleness checked on infinitesimal neighbourhoods (More on Morphisms of Spaces, Lemma spaces-more-morphisms-lemma-check-smoothness-on-infinitesimal-nbhds)
core_obligations: Prove that in the situation of the dilatations theorem, f : X' -> X is etale if and only if g : W -> X_{/T} is etale
proof_roadmap: One direction is quoted from lemma-map-completions-etale.
Conversely, f is an isomorphism over U hence etale there; it remains to check etaleness at points over T.

With Z the reduced closed subspace on T and X_{/T} = colim Z_n, the base changes f^{-1}(Z_n) = X' x_X Z_n -> Z_n are etale because they identify with the base changes of the etale g; the infinitesimal criterion for etaleness then shows f is etale over T.
difficulty_reason: H3: an infinitesimal-neighbourhood argument reducing etaleness over the closed part to the formal etaleness of g.
